title: Second-stage cost alternatives
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$, let $M$ be a positive integer, and let the query state consist of an active family, possibly absent, and an estimate trace. For every output and cost pair in the support of the second-stage program’s run on $f$, either its cost is zero in all three components, or there is a nonempty active family whose cardinality is at most the active cap at threshold $\varepsilon/(4M)$ and the cost is exactly that of the finite-family Fourier estimator using the prescribed sample count at accuracy $\varepsilon$ and confidence $1/20$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional cube
A query state with an optional active family and an estimate trace
The output and cost pair is in the run’s support
